summary.title: COLLEAGUE.SKILL: Automated AI Skill Generation via Expert Knowledge Distillation

setting_and_object.category: Software/system artifact (open-source pipeline for agent-skill generation)

details: Actionable knowledge about a person or role (a teammate's review standards, a public figure's mental models, private interaction patterns) lives in heterogeneous traces, not clean instructions; existing memory/persona systems hide it and skill standards only specify packaging, leaving no end-to-end trace-to-skill workflow.

COLLEAGUE.SKILL: an automated 'person-grounded trace-to-skill distillation' system that turns collected traces of a person/role into a versioned, Agent-Skills-compatible package S = (files, metadata, lifecycle state).

Defining mechanism: distillation into two separately invocable tracks -- a capability track (practices, mental models, decision heuristics) and a bounded behavior track (style, interaction rules, correction log) -- rendered as inspectable files with manifest/meta, plus a natural-language correction loop that patches sections or appends {scene, wrong, correct} records, bumps a version, and supports rollback.
Framing claim is artifact-level (portable, inspectable, composable, correctable, governable), explicitly not behavioral cloning or identity replacement.
Schema version 3 metadata: identity, preset family, source context, classification, artifact names, engine/toolchain, provenance, lifecycle state, compatibility.

Rendered files: SKILL.md (combined entrypoint with frontmatter, user-invocable: true, Part A capability / Part B behavior), work.md and persona.md (editable sources), work_skill.md and persona_skill.md (split entrypoints), manifest.json and meta.json.
Follows Agent Skills standard and progressive disclosure (metadata first, instructions on invocation).

Three presets over one shared pipeline: colleague (primary; enterprise/work traces), celebrity/public-figure (public first-person evidence, source boundaries), relationship (private traces, consent/local-control defaults).
Each preset defines source boundary, storage root, command aliases, prompt bundle, and optional research/safety tooling; new presets (self, author, team) would be configuration plus prompt design.
Collectors/parsers for Feishu, DingTalk, Slack, WeChat SQLite exports, email archives, PDFs, screenshots, Markdown, direct paste.

Celebrity preset adds a six-dimensional research pass (first-person works, long-form interviews, documented decisions, expression style, reception, timeline) with subtitle download, audio transcription, subtitle cleanup, note merging, and a quality checker for mental-model coverage, limitations, tensions, grounding URLs, and copyright signals.
Installation targets: Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex, Hermes.

Correction handler routes feedback to a Markdown patch (level-2 heading match replaces, else appends) or a normalized behavior correction record; writer archives current version, applies change, increments version, regenerates derived artifacts.
Version manager lists archives, backs up, rolls back, cleans old archives.
Public site plus opt-in gallery as distribution layer, with submitter attestation, review, takedown, and source-boundary labels.
No task-performance, fidelity, or human-subject study; the paper explicitly defers these and observes only public deployment counters on 2026-05-28.
Proposed future protocol: compare full vs capability-only vs behavior-only artifacts under matched source evidence.

key_findings.finding: Person-grounded skill construction can be formulated and implemented as an artifact problem rather than as persona prompting, yielding a concrete package format with five operational properties.
key_findings.evidence: The paper defines S = (A, M, L) with portability, inspectability, composability, correctability, and governability, and implements it as a schema-v3 writer emitting SKILL.md, work.md, persona.md, split sub-skills, manifest.json, and meta.json aligned with the Agent Skills spec.

key_findings.finding: Separating capability from bounded behavior into distinct, independently invocable entrypoints makes extraction claims inspectable at file level and lets users use expertise without style transfer.
key_findings.evidence: work.md/work_skill.md carry procedures, standards, review criteria and heuristics while persona.md/persona_skill.md carry style, interaction posture, boundaries and correction log; the paper argues this addresses persona-system failures that conflate factual knowledge, procedural judgment, and surface tone, e.g. work-only invocation of a code-review checklist.

key_findings.finding: Natural-language feedback can be operationalized as a versioned correction lifecycle rather than ad hoc prompt editing.
key_findings.evidence: Correction handler converts feedback such as 'he would not say that' into either a Markdown section patch (heading-matched replacement, otherwise append) or a {scene, wrong, correct} record; the writer archives, applies, increments lifecycle version, regenerates derived artifacts, with list/backup/rollback/clean operations.

key_findings.finding: The same distillation-and-packaging mechanism generalizes across evidence and consent regimes via presets, so governance requirements become configuration rather than new systems.
key_findings.evidence: colleague, celebrity, and relationship presets share the artifact contract while differing in source boundary, prompt bundle, research/quality tooling, consent defaults, and publication rules; the celebrity quality checker enforces grounding URLs and limitations, and the relationship preset makes deletion, local ownership, and non-public defaults first-order requirements.

key_findings.finding: The artifact pipeline has an externally observable public distribution surface, though this is reported only as deployment evidence and not adoption quality.
key_findings.evidence: On 2026-05-28 the authors observed roughly 18.5k GitHub stars and gallery counters of 215 skills, 55 meta-skills, 165 contributors, and more than 100k cumulative gallery stars (reported at order-of-magnitude due to asynchronous syncing).
